blocks.text: 1. Self-Attention

blocks.alt: Position 1, 2, and 3 all attend to all positions

blocks.text: Additive Attention, the previous topic, offered an alternative scoring approach for comparing Query and Key vectors. Self-Attention applies these scoring approaches within a single sequence rather than between two, explored throughout this topic.
It works by having every position genuinely attend to every other position within the exact same sequence, a genuinely important, distinctive extension covered throughout the rest of this topic.
2. Recapping The Two-Sequence Setup
This connects back to Encoder-Decoder Attention, already covered in its own topic. That earlier topic genuinely connected two different sequences: the encoder's input and the decoder's output.
Self-Attention genuinely operates within just one single sequence instead, a genuinely important structural difference explored throughout the rest of this topic.
3. The Core Idea

blocks.alt: Query, key, and value all come from the same sequence

blocks.text: Self-Attention's genuinely core idea connects back to Query, Key, and Value, already covered in their own topic. Every position in a sequence genuinely produces its own Query, Key, and Value, all from that exact same sequence.

This is a genuinely direct, elegant extension of that earlier framework, applied here entirely within one sequence rather than across the two genuinely separate sequences already covered in Encoder-Decoder Attention.

blocks.text: 4. Every Position Attends To All Others

blocks.alt: Word 1 and word 2 both connect into word 3

blocks.text: This connects back to direct access to all positions, already covered in Why Attention. Each position's own Query genuinely gets compared against every single Key in the entire sequence, including itself.
This produces a genuinely rich, context-aware representation for every single position, directly extending the direct-access idea already covered there to now apply entirely within a single sequence.
5. Context-Aware Representations

blocks.alt: A word alone is compared against a word blended with context

blocks.text: This connects forward to Word Embeddings, covered later in this course. A word's own meaning often genuinely depends on its surrounding context within the same sentence.
Self-Attention genuinely lets each word's own representation directly incorporate that surrounding context, a genuinely powerful capability explored further in complete depth in that later module.
6. A Genuine Parallelization Benefit

blocks.alt: RNN processes sequentially while self-attention processes in parallel

blocks.text: This connects back to processing one time step at a time, already covered in Time Steps. Unlike Vanilla RNN, LSTM, and GRU, all already covered, Self-Attention genuinely does not require strictly sequential, step-by-step processing.

Every position's own computation can genuinely happen simultaneously, a genuinely major practical advantage that directly addresses the sequential-processing limitation already covered throughout the RNN and LSTM & GRU modules.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This parallelization benefit, already covered in this topic, is one of the single most important, practical reasons Self-Attention-based architectures, covered later in this course, could train so much faster on modern hardware.

blocks.text: 7. Handling Long-Range Dependencies

This connects back to long-range dependencies genuinely failing, already covered in The Vanishing Gradient Problem. Self-Attention genuinely connects any two positions directly, regardless of how far apart they are.

This directly solves the long-range dependency struggle already covered as Vanilla RNN's own genuine weakness, since there is no longer any genuinely long chain of intermediate steps for information to pass through.
8. A Genuine Computational Cost Consideration

blocks.alt: A sequence length n gives a quadratic cost of n squared

blocks.text: A genuinely honest, real tradeoff connects back to computing every pairwise comparison, already covered in this topic. Comparing every position against every other position genuinely costs computation that grows with the square of sequence length.
This is a genuinely real, honest cost worth acknowledging directly, since the genuinely powerful direct-connection benefit already covered in the previous section does not come entirely for free.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing Why Self-Attention Is Genuinely Such A Significant Development

blocks.alt: Needing global context within one sequence points toward self-attention

blocks.text: This connects back to genuinely needing to process a sequence in parallel, already covered in this topic. Self-Attention, already covered in this topic, directly enables that genuinely major efficiency gain.

This connects forward to Transformers, covered later in this course, built almost entirely from this exact mechanism. Self-Attention, already covered, is genuinely the single most important building block there.
10. Worked Example

The example below directly demonstrates computing Self-Attention for a genuinely small sequence, with every position producing its own Query, Key, and Value from the same sequence, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
sequence_length = 4
hidden_size = 4

sequence = rng.normal(size=(sequence_length, hidden_size))  # a genuinely small sequence, already covered in this topic

# already covered as the core idea in this topic: every position produces its own Query, Key, Value
W_query = rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1
W_key = rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1
W_value = rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1

queries = sequence @ W_query.T
keys = sequence @ W_key.T
values = sequence @ W_value.T

def softmax(x):
    exp_x = np.exp(x - np.max(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True))
    return exp_x / exp_x.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True)

# already covered as every position attends to all others in this topic
scores = queries @ keys.T / np.sqrt(hidden_size)  # already covered as Scaled Dot-Product Attention
attention_weights = softmax(scores)
output = attention_weights @ values

print(f"Attention weights shape (each row sums to 1): {attention_weights.shape}")
print(f"Position 0 attends to: {np.round(attention_weights[0], 3)}")
print(f"\nOutput shape (already covered as context-aware representations in this topic): {output.shape}")

blocks.content: Running this example shows every single position producing an attention distribution over the entire sequence, including itself, exactly the every-position-attends-to-all-others mechanism already covered as this topic's own core idea.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Self-Attention lets every position in a sequence attend to every other position in that same sequence.
This differs from Encoder-Decoder Attention, which connects two genuinely separate sequences.
Every position produces its own Query, Key, and Value, all from that same sequence.
Each position's Query gets compared against every Key in the sequence, including itself.
This produces context-aware representations, incorporating surrounding meaning directly.
Unlike Vanilla RNN, LSTM, and GRU, it does not require strictly sequential processing.
It connects any two positions directly, solving the long-range dependency struggle.
Its computational cost grows with the square of sequence length, a genuine, honest tradeoff.
Next up: Cross-Attention, a closer contrast between attending within one sequence versus between two.
